why_trail.why: Handoff is complete and the one derivation it handed me to settle is confirmed by measurement: the server script's own location resolves to the same primary checkout the incumbent SPINE_FILE-based derivation returns, while also answering when nothing is bound. The shape of the work is now fixed: SPINE and SESSION become late-bound module state with a single named binder; the three telemetry paths become functions that keep their env overrides and answer None when unbound; _primary_checkout_for_lifecycle stops reading os.environ.

The regression test is committed-ready and demonstrably fails on the defective tree for the right reason, so the fix that follows cannot pass it by accident. Writing it first also settled the refusal CONTRACT the implementation must now meet: two message shapes (unbound names no path and points at spine_open; bound-but-unusable names the path and says how to rebind), 10 of 11 tools refusing, and spine_open reachable as the single escape hatch.

Fail-closed landed as one class with two messages. The design call I owned -- where the check sits -- resolved to the tools/call dispatch in main(), ahead of every per-tool required-argument check, so an unbound door answers the question the caller actually has rather than a downstream complaint about an argument that would not have helped; run_engine asks the SAME predicate again as defense in depth for the pass-through path, which also removes the '--file None' argv that would otherwise be constructed. Three committed tests encoded the OLD fail-open mechanism and were reconciled deliberately, each keeping its claim and changing only its mechanism: test_mcp_door_engine_cwd's removed-spine-directory test now asserts a refusal that never reaches the engine while still proving the process neither moves nor dies, and the two DC3 controls in test_mcp_identity now assert a REFUSAL rather than a crash -- strictly more evidence for DC3, since a crash proves only the absence of an answer while a refusal proves the door was reachable, had no identity, and did not read the parent's.

Bind-on-open reached WITHOUT weakening _identity_violation -- the stop condition did not fire. The guard compares against SPINE at call time, so moving the binding left it strictly intact, and four new tests measure that rather than assume it. Both identity roots move together: claim succeeding in the transcript is what proves SESSION was rebound, not just SPINE. The rebind is refused while this process holds an active lease, checked BEFORE open_work so a refusal never leaves a real branch and worktree behind. ONE departure from the handoff's preferred answer, forced by measurement and not by preference: deriving the primary checkout from Path(__file__) OUTRIGHT is wrong, because it silently redirects spine_open into whichever checkout the SCRIPT lives in. Measured -- under the outright replacement, tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py FullStdioRoundTripTests created the branch and worktree 'roundtrip-work' in the developer's REAL checkout and still passed, because spine_close tidied up after itself. I removed that worktree and branch and verified the repo is clean. The correct shape is bound-spine-first with the script's location as the FALLBACK when nothing is bound: identical answers in production (measured both ways), unchanged isolation for every existing caller, and it still answers the case the old form could not answer at all. This is not the fourth ambient input the stop condition guards against -- no new environment variable, no cwd read -- so I proceeded rather than stopping, and recorded it here and in the function's own docstring.

The :194 ban survives byte-identical -- verified by extracting BANNED_IDENTIFIERS, _referenced_names, both test methods and the whole enclosing class from the 408e6d26 tree and from this one and comparing them byte for byte, all five IDENTICAL, and it still passes. The new module-wide pin is strictly stronger and demonstrably capable of failing: mutating the REAL server with a second rebind site (_quietly_retarget_the_session doing 'global SESSION; SESSION = ...') turns the new pin RED while the :194 ban stays GREEN under the identical mutation -- which is the concrete demonstration that a function-scoped ban structurally cannot see a second rebind site elsewhere in the module, and therefore that adding rather than rewriting was the right call. The detector counts AnnAssign, AugAssign, walrus, for/with/except targets and not just ast.Assign, because enumerating one assignment shape is the same shape-guessing this repo's identity guards were defeated by six times. Source restored byte-identical after the mutation.

The demo default is gone, so an interactive session that sets nothing now lands on a refusal that names spine_open rather than on a demo spine's answers presented as its own. The full clean-env suite is green -- 3093 passed, 6 skipped, 1153 subtests, 0 failed. One extra reconciliation the handoff did not list but its constraints did anticipate: map/INDEX.md went stale because this gate adds entities (_spine_from_env, _engine_from_env, _telemetry_path, _calllog, _start_marker, _rejectionlog, _unbound_refusal, _bind_process_to, _rebind_refusal), so I rebuilt it with py -m scripts.code_map build --root . and it is committed with the change.

Every new symbol is wired to a production call site -- the shipped-inert failure this gate could not afford did not happen, and the two that carry the gate's whole meaning (_bind_process_to from _spine_open, _unbound_refusal from main's dispatch and run_engine) are the best-wired of the twelve. The three telemetry overrides survive the late-binding, measured live rather than reasoned about. The change is committed as 4e1f22cb with the rebuilt code map, the working tree is clean of source changes, and the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT is written to the path the handoff names -- left uncommitted, per the handoff's Deliverable path check marking everything under .agent-work/ local-only.
